scope: Email has simple one-key commands and pages with a clear start and end. F9 turns the microphone off. The media player menu opens only with Alt.

topics.title: Turn the microphone off
details: Press F9 to turn the microphone fully off. Voice Companion then hears nothing, not even Wake up.
Press F9 again to turn it back on. F9 works on every screen.
You can also say Turn off the microphone.

topics.title: One key for each email action
details: In the message list and in an open message, press one letter. No other keys are needed.
N is new email. R is reply. A is reply all. F is forward.
M moves a message. G goes to a folder. W says which folder you are in.
I reads message details. C copies the sender address. E writes to the sender.
D opens email drafts. P lists contacts. S says what is selected. U clears the marks.
The Email menu shows each key. The older keys still work.

topics.title: Print Screen goes to the main menu
details: Press Print Screen on any screen to go back to the main menu.
If a document has changes, you are asked to save it first.
If Print Screen opens the Windows screen capture tool, turn that off. Open Windows Settings, then Accessibility, then Keyboard.

topics.title: Pages of email
details: Up Arrow and Down Arrow now stop at the first and last message on the page. You hear Start of list or End of list.
Page Down and Page Up go to the next or previous page of messages.
Home and End go to the first and last message on this page.
Control+Home and Control+End go to the newest and oldest message in the folder.

topics.title: Media player
details: While a file plays, only Alt opens the player menu.
Escape now leaves the player and goes back to the folder the file came from.
Each Escape after that goes up one folder. From the drive list, Escape goes to the Media menu, then the main menu.
Enter plays or pauses, like Space. Home goes back to the start of the file.

topics.title: Reading keys
details: Control+R reads a whole draft, note, or file in the Document reader. In a lesson, Control+R repeats it.
Control+E explains a command in a lesson.
In a document, Control+Shift+R still reads it, because Control+R places text on the right.
